newsitem.title: USA: World sugar use record 125 mln tonnes 1997/98-USDA.
newsitem.headline: World sugar use record 125 mln tonnes 1997/98-USDA.

text.p: World sugar consumption in 1997/98 was forecast to rise to a record 125 million tonnes, the U.S. Agriculture Department said Friday.
The figure would be two percent larger than the current year and six percent above 1995/96.
"Stronger demand is likely in many chief consuming countries, especially those in Asia and South America," USDA said in its periodic "Sugar: World Markets and Trade" report.
USDA repeated its estimates from earlier this month of sugar production of 122.4 million tonnes in 1997/98 and record world sugar trade of 36 million tonnes.

Forecast for sugar production in 1996/97 was reduced to 122.3 million tons, a drop of 2.6 million tonnes. India accounted for most of the decline due to lower cane yields and increased diversion of cane to making other sweeteners.
Trade in sugar in 1996/97 was estimated at 35.8 million tonnes, up one percent from the previous estimate. Larger exportable supplies in Thailand and European Union accounted for the increase.
For 1997/98, record output was expected in Central and South America, such as Brazil and Guatemala. Records also were possible in South Africa, Thailand, Turkey, Egypt, Australia.

The predicted surge in consumption in 1997/98 "is due to a mix of factors, including higher consumer incomes, population growth and rising consumer demand for sugar-containing products such as soft drinks and processed foods," USDA said.
USDA left its forecast of 1996/97 consumption unchanged at 122.8 million tonnes.
